object.title: Archer et al.'s quasi-Stirling descent conjecture
object.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}=\{1^2,2^2,\ldots,n^2\}$, and let $\overline{\mathcal{Q}}_{\mathcal{M}}$ denote the set of quasi-Stirling permutations of $\mathcal{M}$. For a permutation $\pi=\pi_1\pi_2\ldots\pi_{2n}$, define

$$
des(\pi)=|\{i\mid \pi_i>\pi_{i+1},\ 1\leq i\leq 2n-1\}|+1.
$$

**Archer et al.'s conjecture.** The number of $\pi\in\overline{\mathcal{Q}}_{\mathcal{M}}$ with $des(\pi)=n$ is equal to

$$
(n+1)^{n-1}.
$$

This conjecture concerns the descent enumerator of quasi-Stirling permutations on the multiset in which every element occurs twice. It refines the known enumeration $|\overline{\mathcal{Q}}_{\mathcal{M}}|=n!C_n$, where $C_n$ is the $n$th Catalan number; the supplied text gives no evidence that the descent-count assertion has been resolved.
object.source_name: Sherry H. F. Yan and Xue Zhu, “Quasi-Stirling Polynomials on Multisets”, arXiv:2106.04347 (2021).
object.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2002.00985](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.00985).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.04347

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).
